title: U.S. global-role legitimacy separates foreign reception, domestic judgment, and partisan meaning
source_unit: Pew 2026 Global Attitudes Survey and U.S. American Trends Panel supplement; country publics and US respondents kept separate

observations.method: Pew cross-country survey as reported in the retained official analysis.
observations.uncertainty: Equal-country median is not a population-weighted global estimate; public perception does not measure government behavior, alliance coordination, or capability.
observations.subgroup: Adults in the 36 surveyed non-US countries.
observations.counterinterpretation: Poor public reception can coexist with continued cooperation or material capability, and positive reception can coexist with disagreement.

observations.period: March 23-29, 2026; U.S. American Trends Panel supplement
observations.method: Pew U.S. supplement as reported in the retained official analysis.
observations.uncertainty: Normative and descriptive judgments are not actual policy outcomes, later action, or validated capability assessments.
observations.subgroup: US adults; each question has its own valid response base.
observations.counterinterpretation: Shared judgment about interference does not imply shared approval or a common policy demand.

denominator.unit: US adults supplement; partisan subgroups have separate valid bases

observations.method: Pew partisan subgroup comparisons from the U.S. supplement.
observations.uncertainty: Partisan differences are descriptive and do not identify event attribution, media cause, stable cohort change, or later political action.
observations.counterinterpretation: Partisans can disagree about legitimacy while sharing a descriptive judgment that the US is highly interventionist.

related_sources.claim: Pew survey frames, global and domestic results, and interpretation limits.
Material capacity and leverage clocks remain separate from legitimacy perception.
Domestic material-to-trust/action records provide a separate political-meaning comparison.

boundary: This is a deliberately non-pooled legitimacy synthesis. It distinguishes foreign reception, domestic judgment, and partisan meaning, but does not estimate a causal policy effect, international reputation trend, alliance response, state capability, geopolitical leverage, or political action from the survey. An event-country-party-year behavior ledger remains open.
